Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

- **Warmest day:** 18°C high on **2025-03-07**
- **Coolest night:** 4°C low on **2025-03-05**
- **Wettest day:** 8 mm rain on **2025-03-04**
- **Most humid day:** 63% on **2025-03-04**

## Best Chart Set for Your Climate Project
### 1) Temperature range chart
- Use a **line chart with two lines**: one for daily high, one for daily low.
- Best for showing the **gap between daytime warmth and nighttime coolness**.
- Add a shaded band between the two lines if your tool supports it.

### 2) Rainfall chart
- Use a **bar chart** for `rain_mm`.
- Best for showing that rain was **concentrated on just a few days**.
- A bar chart makes the jump on **March 4** easy to spot.

### 3) Humidity chart
- Use a **line chart** or **bar chart** for `humidity_pct`.
- Best for showing the **rise in moisture during the rainy middle of the week**.
- A line chart works well if you want to compare it visually with temperature trends.

### 4) Optional combined view
- Use a **dual-axis chart** with:
  - temperature on the left axis
  - rainfall or humidity on the right axis
- Good if you want **one compact figure** instead of three separate charts.

## Data Pattern in Plain Language
- Madrid was **mild and fairly dry overall** during this week.
- Temperatures dipped in the middle of the week, then **warmed up again by March 7**.
- Rain was **light to moderate and short-lived**, with the biggest rain event on **March 4**.
- Humidity moved up when rain increased, then **dropped again as the weather dried out**.

### Quick interpretation sentence
This week looks like a **cool, mostly dry early spring pattern**, with a brief **rainy and more humid midweek period** followed by **clearer, warmer conditions** at the end.
